recipes.name: Kansas Baked Beans
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 (16 ounce) can butter beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add bacon, ground beef, and onion; cook until bacon and ground beef completely browned, 7 to 10 minutes. Drain any excess fat; transfer to a casserole dish.

Stir white sugar, brown sugar, ketchup, barbecue sauce, mustard, molasses, chili powder, and black pepper together in a bowl; pour over bacon mixture. Add pork and beans, kidney beans, and butter beans; mix thoroughly.
Bake in the preheated oven until liquid thickens, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Kansas Baked Beans
raw_recipe.description: Three beans, bacon, beef, sugar, ketchup, barbecue sauce, mustard, molasses, and chili powder make this sweet, spicy Kansas baked beans recipe perfect.

review.reviewBody: Super easy!! I made it for after church in the crockpot and used Busch's baked homestyle beans! Minus the brown sugar, it was a huge hit! Will definitely make it again!

This is my go- to recipe now for "baked beans" I put 2 cups of presoaked dry pinto or bolita beans in to the crockpot on high with some chicken broth, cook them until done, about 4 hours. Then I drain the beans, reserving the liquid to put back as needed. Put the beans back into the crockpot with the seasonings. I omit the white sugar, I double the kechup and BBQ sauce, add about a teaspoon of minced garlic (I like garlic!) Heat for about another hour or so until the flavors blend. Sometimes I omit the bacon and burger. Comes out perfect! Nice sweet-spicey flavor.

I added 1/2 lb of sweet Italian sausage, 1 crushed clove of garlic, doubled the amount of ketchup, BBQ sauce, and molasses. Cooked covered in oven @ 275 for 4 hours, stirring every hour. Absolutely fabulous! My book club raved about it. NOTE: Brown bacon first, and put aside. Then brown beef, sausage, garlic and onion, and mix with bacon. Otherwise beef, sausage and onion will burn while you wait for bacon to cook.

Best baked beans I've ever had. I took the advice of others. Double the ketchup and mustard, triple the BBQ sauce. You can always continue to bake if it is still too wet, mine was perfect. I am not a big fan of butter beans so switched with white kidney beans. Used half the chili seasoning (for my daughter). I also like a little tartness from vinegar, I used a BBQ sauce with that flavor profile with was fantastic.

My family loved this recipe. I mixed it exactly as written but cooked them in the crockpot and they were a huge hit at the family barbecue. This recipe makes quite a large amount and the small amount leftover were great the next day. I plan to make them again for the upcoming Memorial weekend. Kudos, great recipe!
I made the recipe and the only change I made was halved the sugar. The next time I will double the sauce & substitute Hillshire ring sausage for the ground beef. Delicious!

These were so hearty and good! I added some sausage to the meat blend and also added 2 Tbsp Worcestershire sauce. We took them to our church small group meeting, and they were an absolute hit! These baked beans (with the slight mods) are our new favorite. I'm already looking forward to making another batch.
Chili Powder gave it too much Cumin flavor to be anything but a Tex Mex taste. I’d use a single pepper powder, as opposed to a combo powder like Chili Powder.
Always a hit at the family BBQ!
Awesome! Big hit at a 4th of July gathering. They caramelized beautifully.

I have made this 4 times this summer! It is the most praised food item at the various gatherings where we have served them. My husband couldn’t care less about beans until I started making these. We have even eaten them as a main dish.

I just read through the recipe, and it is exactly the same as a recipe I already have, but by a different name. This recipe is so yummy! My husband asks for it over other bean recipes I've made. I have shared this recipe, and the friend I shared it with calls it Sweet Chili. This is great for potlucks, and makes great leftovers.
made this in a "keto" version. it came out amazing. will definitely make again.

Do not torture yourself by waiting until the next day to eat these beans. They are delicious right out of the crock pot. Makes a huge batch so leftovers are there for the next day. I did make my own barbecue sauce and added additional to leftovers when heating up to thin out a bit. This is a fantastic bean recipe.
Very good! Big hit at the pot luck!
I followed the recipe exactly and it was delicious! Everyone raves about how good it was. I would definitely make this again!
